=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: Lines 517-523 (LAST RUN DIFF hunk — try/except ApiError around post-create _list_digest) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the post-create digest listing fails transiently, older is silently set to None and the code returns the newly created digest as the park destination. If a real older concurrent digest existed before the listing failure, the new duplicate digest is never closed. The subsequent park calls, which always select the oldest digest via find_digest, update only the correct oldest one, leaving the duplicate open with a stale entry indefinitely.
  WHY: If GitHub is experiencing partial degradation (rate limiting, intermittent 5xx), each concurrent park that suffers a failed post-create listing leaves behind an open duplicate digest issue. Over time, multiple duplicates can accumulate with stale entries. No code path ever closes duplicates that were created during a period where the older-digest check failed. The impact is benign (no items are lost and the scan still works correctly) but the duplicate issues are operational noise and waste issue numbers.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: Lines 517-523, the except ApiError block | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No diagnostic log is emitted when the post-create listing fails. The _needs_human_log call at line 529 logs "parked" identically whether the duplicate check succeeded or failed, so operators cannot distinguish "no older digest existed" from "listing failed, a duplicate may still be open."
  WHY: If GitHub is rate-limiting, parks silently take the "no older digest" branch with no operational signal. Operators would see successful parks in the log but would not know that duplicate digests are accumulating or that API health is degraded.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 517-523 (`except ApiError: older = None` after the digest creation in `_needs_human_park_digest`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new `try/except ApiError` around the post-create `_list_digest` call silently swallows the failure and the in-code comment is incorrect. It claims "A duplicate digest left open here is merged on a later park (the oldest one wins)" but the merge logic (`if older is not None and int(older.get("number") or 0) < number:`) only fires when `_list_digest` actually returns a digest — and that branch is only reached inside the `digest is None` arm of the retry loop. When both writers (A creates #900, B creates #901) hit transient API failures on their second listing, the helper returns `newly_parked=True` for both, but no code path ever closes #901.
  WHY: After the race, the system has two open digests (`ai:operator-step`). All future `park` and `prune` calls go to the OLDEST (#900) because `find_digest` returns the lowest-numbered candidate. The newer #901 is invisible to the runtime but stays open. The entries that should have lived in #900 but landed in #901 are absent from `parse_digest`'s output (the poller's prune reads #900's body), so the unblock scan does not see those items as parked. The scan then judges them again, and the judge parks them in #900, producing a second CRITICAL alert for items that were "already" parked in #901. The test the editor added (`test_needs_human_digest_park_reports_the_park_when_the_post_create_listing_fails`) only forces the second listing to fail when no older digest exists; it does not seed an existing older digest the way `test_needs_human_digest_park_merges_into_an_older_concurrent_digest` does, so the regression is not pinned.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: lines 517-523 (the `except ApiError: older = None` branch) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the post-create `_list_digest` raises `ApiError`, the error is silently dropped. No `_needs_human_log` line is emitted and no exception is re-raised, so an operator watching `NEEDS_HUMAN` lines cannot distinguish a real "no older digest exists" case from a transient GitHub rate-limit / 5xx.
  WHY: If GitHub is rate-limiting or partially down, every concurrent park silently takes the "no older" branch. The duplicate digest leak above is then produced without any operational signal, making the regression much harder to detect from logs.
- Requirement: "Adds or updates the item's line (item number, kind, stop reason, link to the last verdict)."
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `needs_human_park_project`, and `scripts/operator_step_issue.py` `render_digest_entry`.
  Evidence of absence: The poller passes `--link "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${TRACKING_NUM}"` with no `#issuecomment-…` anchor. The renderer's link-label rule (`'last verdict' if '#issuecomment-' in link else 'details'`) therefore emits `[details](…)` rather than `[last verdict](…)` for every poller-parked project. No branch of `needs_human_park_project` resolves the last verdict URL for projects (it only fires when `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_ENABLED=false`, so no verdict comment exists), so the digest entries carry the tracking-issue URL labelled "details" — which the linked issue explicitly distinguished from "link to the last verdict".
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: `_needs_human_park_digest`, lines 517-523 (LAST RUN DIFF hunk wrapping post-create `_list_digest` in try/except ApiError) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the post-create listing fails transiently, `older` is set to None and the code returns `newly_parked=True` with the just-created digest's number. The in-code comment promises "A duplicate digest left open here is merged on a later park (the oldest one wins)", but that merge logic only fires on the create path when `older is not None and int(older.get("number") or 0) < number`. Once a park goes to the existing-digest branch, no code path closes a newer duplicate.
  WHY: After a transient listing failure, if a real older concurrent digest exists, the next park for any item calls `_list_digest` which returns the oldest pipeline-authored digest. That older digest gets the new entry, but the newer duplicate created during the failure is never closed. It remains open indefinitely with stale entries. Items in the duplicate are absent from prune's returned `items`, so the unblock scan judges and parks those items again into the older digest, producing repeated CRITICAL alerts until the duplicate is manually closed. The impact is cosmetic (a second digest with stale entries) and self-correcting over time, but contradicts the in-code comment and wastes one CRITICAL alert per re-parked item.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: `_needs_human_park_digest`, the try/except around post-create `_list_digest` (LAST RUN DIFF hunk at lines 517-523) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the post-create listing fails with ApiError, `older` is silently set to None with no log line. Operators cannot distinguish a transient GitHub API failure from a real "no older digest exists" outcome.
  WHY: If GitHub is rate-limiting or partially down, every park silently takes the "no older" branch and may leave duplicate digests open with no operational signal in the NEEDS_HUMAN log stream. The workflow log shows `outcome=parked` with no indication that the verification step degraded. A single `_needs_human_log(item, kind, "post_create_listing_failed", "parked")` call before setting `older = None` would surface the degradation without changing behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
